Castleton (grid square 1582, confirmed by pixel gridline detection: vertical gridlines at x=852('15')/1201('16'), horizontal at y=780('83')/1132('82'), village label falls inside that box) sits on the floor of a valley: Peakshole Water (blue stream) runs past/through it, the main A625-type road (drawn in pink/red) runs the length of the dale through the village, and densely packed contours rise on both sides (steeply south into Cave Dale, and further north/NW into the Woodseats/Hollins hillside). This matches option 0 exactly; the other three options (exposed high ground, complete woodland cover, coastal harbour) are all contradicted by the map.

The road runs east-west along the valley floor through squares 1483/1583/1582, where contour density is very low (pixel counts ~3-5 crossings per km) -- i.e. flat, gentle going. Contours are far denser (20-30 crossings per km) in the hillside squares such as 1384 to the north(-west). Widely-spaced contours on the valley floor vs tightly packed ones on higher ground is the real reason roads hug valley floors. Options 1-3 are all false on this map (no wall-to-wall woodland on the fells, more than one stream is shown, and the road does not slavishly trace the river).
answers.concerns: The squares immediately bordering the road to the north (1483, 1583) are themselves quite flat too -- the really tight packing only appears roughly 1-1.5 km further north/NW (square 1384). Option 0 is still clearly the best-supported of the four choices, but 'the ground to the north' is a slight simplification of where the steep contours actually start.
